title: Pomegranate Honey Vinaigrette
changes_from_base: Same steep-then-whisk method as the classic shallot vinaigrette, with pomegranate molasses, garlic and a little honey added for a sweet-sour, deep red dressing; no mayonnaise.
summary: Shallot and garlic mellowed in cider vinegar, then whisked with pomegranate molasses, honey, mustard and olive oil into a glossy, deep red dressing.
equipment: whisk or jar with a lid

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Mellow the shallot
steps.text: Put the shallot, garlic and salt in the bowl, pour over the cider vinegar and leave for 10 min so the shallot loses its raw bite.

steps.title: Make the sweet-sour base
steps.text: Whisk in the pomegranate molasses, honey, mustard and pepper until the molasses has dissolved and the mixture looks even.

steps.title: Emulsify
steps.text: Whisking all the time, add the olive oil in a thin stream until the dressing turns glossy and slightly thick. You can also shake everything hard in a lidded jar for about 20 seconds.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Dress crisp leaves, sliced tomatoes, grilled aubergine or a herb and bread salad just before eating. Whisk again if it separates.

tips: Taste your pomegranate molasses first: if it is very sharp, add a little more honey; if it is very sweet, leave the honey out.
A pinch of sumac or ground cumin suits it well.
It makes a good glaze brushed over grilled halloumi or roasted carrots.
storage: Store in a sealed jar in the fridge for up to 1 week. Bring to room temperature and shake well before using. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
